synopsis: Capture infrastructure now starts its command in a dedicated process session and terminates that process group on timeout or interrupted capture. Synthetic preflight passed9 checks including a timed-out parent whose grandchild must not write its delayed sentinel.

criteria.evidence: Success, stderr/failure, assertion, malformed parsing, resumed text, preview analogue, automatic-return analogue, blocked report and timeout descendant check all passed.

recommendations: Use existing receipt-only capture interface with bounded timeout. No command exception text or protected output enters receipt.
Process-group cleanup only targets descendants in that newly created session; do not use it to terminate unrelated owner/system processes.
limitations: No OS-enforced reader isolation claimed. Shared filesystem remains procedural access boundary.
Synthetic marker controls do not replace semantic review of reports or native capture redaction.
Process groups cannot guarantee cleanup of a child that deliberately detaches into another session; no such behavior was tested or claimed.
Change was loaded only by subsequent wrapper executions; already running Python captures kept their original in-memory implementation.
